title: S3 -- lifecycle, versioning, presigned URLs, events
exp: S3 looks simple but has depth that matters for production. Lifecycle rules, versioning, and event notifications directly affect cost and automation.
pts: Storage classes: Standard (frequent), Standard-IA (45% cheaper), Glacier (68% cheaper), Deep Archive (95% cheaper).
Lifecycle rules: automatically transition objects to cheaper classes or delete after N days.
Versioning: keeps all versions; accidental deletes can be recovered.
Presigned URL: time-limited URL granting temporary access without AWS credentials.
S3 Event Notifications: trigger Lambda/SQS when an object is created -- event-driven pipelines.
code:
import boto3
s3 = boto3.client('s3', region_name='us-east-1')

resp = s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket='my-bucket', Prefix='data/orders/2024/')
for obj in resp.get('Contents', []): print(obj['Key'], obj['Size'])

s3.upload_file('local.parquet', 'my-bucket', 'data/output.parquet',
               ExtraArgs={'ServerSideEncryption': 'AES256'})

url = s3.generate_presigned_url('get_object',
    Params={'Bucket':'my-bucket','Key':'reports/q4.pdf'}, ExpiresIn=3600)

s3.put_bucket_lifecycle_configuration(
    Bucket='my-bucket',
    LifecycleConfiguration={'Rules':[{
        'ID':'ArchiveOldData','Status':'Enabled','Prefix':'data/orders/',
        'Transitions':[{'Days':90,'StorageClass':'GLACIER_IR'}],
        'Expiration':{'Days':365}}]})

viz.note: Storage cost ladder: Standard ($0.023/GB) -> Standard-IA ($0.0125) -> Glacier Instant ($0.004) -> Deep Archive ($0.00099). Lifecycle rules move data down as it ages.

qa.q: What is an S3 lifecycle rule and when is it essential?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** A lifecycle rule auto-transitions objects to cheaper storage or deletes after N days. Without it, data accumulates in S3 Standard indefinitely. Standard-IA is 45% cheaper for infrequent access, Glacier Deep Archive 95% cheaper for archives. Lifecycle rules are the primary S3 cost control mechanism.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Message brokers persist events to partitioned append-only logs or in-memory queues, enabling distributed pub/sub with consumer groups.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Poison pill messages without dead-letter queues (DLQ) block partition processing and trigger infinite retry loops.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Partitioned event streaming (Kafka) guarantees order per key at scale, but partition rebalancing incurs consumer pause latency.

**Elevator Pitch:** A URL encoding AWS credentials and a signature, granting temporary access to a private object without AWS credentials. After ExpiresIn seconds it returns 403. Use to share reports with external partners without making the bucket public.
